name: Bear Valley Group Campground
description: pBear Valley Group Camping Area is an ideal location to enjoy incredible scenery and a multitude of outdoor activities in Northern California. Located close to rivers, lakes and trails, the campground welcomes up to 100 people at a time for day use and up to 50 people at a time for overnight camping. The nearby Bear river and South Yuba river offer recreation opportunities. Multiple lakes including Fuller, Rucker, Spaulding and Lake Valley provide plenty of choices for swimmers, boaters and anglers to get out and enjoy the water. Additional use fees may apply at these and other nearby facilities and are not included in the Bear Valley Group Camping fees. The Sierra Discovery Trail winds through the head of Bear Valley along the Bear River where a small waterfall is one of the highlights, and a picnic area lets you stop and take in the scenery while taking a break. Interpretive signs and a kiosk are located at the trailhead. Food PreparationDining Facilities Built-in BBQ, food prepserving tables, picnic-table seating for up to 100 people, potable water and ice-machine at the adjacent pump house, bear-proof food lockers, electrical outlets for small appliances, (no RV hook-ups), dumpster for trash disposal, and area lighting is provided. Camping Amenities Tent camping on designated lawn areas (NO CAMPING ON MAIN LAWN) and in wooded areas, adjacent overflow parking areas. Paved, level parking for multiple RV's, (no hook-ups), Potable water spigots and two double vault toilet facilities are also on-site. Bear-proof food lockers keep your groceries safe, while a built-in barbecue, prep. tables, serving tables, and picnic-table seating help feed a crowd. For entertainment, there are horseshoe pits, a sand volleyball court (bring your own net) and a group fire pit to gather around. Reservations are made through our on-line system.p

name: Big Pine River Access and Camping Dispersed
description: Big Pine River Access and Camping Dispersed has four campsites in this remote campground. Located on the Pit River in Northern California's Shasta County. You can enjoy fishing, hiking and other outdoor recreation. Big Pine is just one of the many campgrounds operated by Pacific Gas and Electric Co.

name: Black Rock Campground Closed for 2026 season
description: pBlack Rock Campground is not reservable. It is First-Come First-Served ONLY. Please select the Opening amp Closing Dates icon to view the season dates. Enjoy the seclusion of Black Rock Campground on the west end of Black Rock Reservoir in the Sierra National Forest. Near the Black Rock Campground is fishing access at the reservoir, which is open year-round. RV's are not allowed and there is NO drinking water or garbage facility. To keep the location as beautiful as you found it, pack it in and pack it out. The family campground is operated by Pacific Gas and Electric Co.p

name: Blue Lake Dispersed Camping
description:
Blue Lake Dispersed Camping is not reservable. It is First-Come First-Serve ONLY. Please select the Opening & Closing Dates icon to view the season dates. 

Blue Lake Dispersed Campground is a remote location that requires high clearance vehicles. 4-wheel drive is recommended. Dispersed camping is available at this hike-in campground operated by Pacific Gas and Electric Co. The entry road is not paved or graded, and there are no restrooms or tables.	 There is no garbage service provided, so please make sure that what you pack in, you pack out. There is no water available here either so, pack enough for cooking, dish-washing and drinking.

name: Carr Feeley Lakes Trailhead and Dispersed Camping
description:
A wealth of lakes are accessible to visitors at Carr-Feeley Lakes Trailhead and Camping in the Tahoe National Forest area. There is an informal boat launch for canoes and hand-carried boats. Activities include fishing, canoeing, boating within a 10 mph limit, swimming, hiking and horseback riding on the trails. Mountain bikers are also able to pedal on roads and some trails. There is a double vault toilet at the trailhead, but no picnic tables. Eleven hike-in campsites are available to campers at the Pacific Gas and Electric Co. facility.

Carr Feeley Lakes Campground  is non-reservable. It is First-come First-serve ONLY. Please select the Opening & Closing Dates icon to view the season dates. There is no garbage service provided, so please make sure that what you pack in, you pack out. There is no water available here either so, pack enough for cooking, dish-washing and drinking.

name: Cassel Campground
description: Cassel Campground offers first-come first-served campsites and reservable campsites. This family campground includes no-hookup campsites, shady pine trees, vault toilets and clean, drinkable water available from multiple faucets. Be sure to pack your fishing gear, nearby Hat Creek is well known for its challenging fly fishing.

name: Cool Springs Campground
description: pEnjoy the outstanding views and tranquil atmosphere at Butt Valley Reservoir when you set up camp at Cool Springs Campground in Northern California's Plumas County. The campground is part of Pacific Gas and Electric Co.'s recreation area which centers around Butt Valley Reservoir, which is surrounded by Forest Service and private timberland. Cool Springs Campground is located on the eastern shore about midway down the lake. The calm waters prove ideal for fishing and kayaking. Boating is allowed at speeds up to 5 mph with a 30' height restriction, including mast. There are no hookups at the campground but it does have vaulted toilet facilities.p

name: Culbertson Lake Dispersed Camping
description: Culbertson Lake is a good location for all types of anglers, whether you are fly fishing, spinning or baitcasting. Three campsites are open for hike-in dispersed camping at the Pacific Gas and Electric Co. facility. There are no restrooms or picnic tables, but plenty of opportunities to explore the Tahoe National Forest.

name: Dusty Campground
description:
Dusty Campground is situated to take advantage of nearby water sports as it lies on the shore of beautiful Lake Britton. This facility is set among shaded trees in the Lassen National Forest. Small boats are allowed at the campground, which includes nine sites. Two are designated for groups of up to 12 campers.  

Dusty Campground is non-reserveable. It is First-Come First-Serve ONLY. Please select the Opening & Closing Dates icon to view the season dates.

name: Fuller Grove Campground
description:
Fuller Grove Campground is non-reservable. It is First-Come First-Serve camping ONLY. Please select the Opening & Closing Dates icon to view the season dates. 

Fuller Grove Campground is located on Lake Pillsbury in the Mendocino National Forest. For lakeside camping, good fishing and boating, it's hard to beat Fuller Grove. The campground has 23 campsites, including six doubles. There are numerous back-country roads in the area providing unlimited potential to observe wildlife. Many mountains, canyons, lakes, rivers and streams are glorious features of the Mendocino National Forest where visitors come for all types of water sports. Activities include hiking, backpacking, boating, fishing and hunting, you can also observe blooming wildflowers in spring and bird-watching within its 913,306 acres.

name: Fuller Grove Group Campground
description:
Fuller Grove Group Campground is located on Lake Pillsbury in the Mendocino National Forest. Many mountains, canyons, lakes, rivers and streams are just some of the glorious features of the Mendocino National Forest where visitors come for all types of recreation. Group campground reservations can comfortably accommodate up to 50 people. 

Area attractions include fishing, boating and water-skiing on the lake. Lake Pillsbury is the largest lake in the forest with 65 miles of shoreline, making for a fun-filled vacation. Light up the individual and group barbecues for fine outdoor grilling and everyone will find a seat at the many picnic tables. Two storage units keep food fresh and secure. RV's may park in the paved area. Boat-ramp parking and a launching facility are located adjacent to Fuller Grove. For lakeside camping, good-fishing and boating, it's hard to beat Fuller Grove Group Campground. 

The campground is open from April to September, giving you the best time of the year to sight-see, play and explore.

name: Grizzly Forebay Campground
description:
CAMP CLOSE for 2021 Season 

At Grizzly Forebay Campground in the Plumas National Forest you will find seven remote walk-in campsites.  The sites are 3/4 of a mile from the parking lot. The parking area has fishing access to Grizzly Forebay and a vault toilet. The lake is great for fishing, boating, swimming, canoeing, rafting and kayaking. The Plumas National Forest located in the Sierra Nevada's, is celebrated for great weather, an abundance of streams and lakes, and spectacular geographic diversity, that runs from deep canyons to spectacular peaks. 

Grizzly Forebay Campground is non-reservable. It is First-Come First-Served ONLY. Please select the Opening & Closing Dates icon to view the season dates.

name: Haskins Valley Campground
description: Set among the beautiful pine trees in a cove at the south end of Bucks Lake, Haskins Valley Campground is a popular vacation spot in California's Plumas County. A portion of the 65 campsites are available through our on-line reservation system. Haskins Valley Campground has a trailer/camper sanitary station, double vault toilets and a nearby courtesy boat ramp at the west end of the campground (associated $10.00 launch fee for non-campers). RV's up to 30 feet in length can be accommodated on a few of the sites, which feature picnic tables, fire rings with grill and potable water. The campground is part of Pacific Gas and Electric Co.'s recreation area which centers around Bucks Lake. The lake has fishing and is a terrific place to swim, boat and water ski.

name: Hawkins Landing Campground and Boat Launch
description:
Hawkins Landing Campground is non-reservable. It is First-Come First-Serve ONLY. Please select the Opening & Closing Dates icon to view the season dates. 

Hawkins Landing Campground and Boat Launch is off the beaten path. Located within Shasta County in Northern California, the small campground offers 10 campsites near the Iron Canyon Reservoir. Powerboats, rowboats, canoes, sailboats and inflatable boats are allowed on the water. Staying at Hawkins Landing Campground is an excellent way to admire the diverse landscape of the Shasta-Trinity National Forest, the largest in California.

name: Hutchins Group Campground
address: Mill Creek Road, USFS Route 24N33 to 24N87X
description:
To make reservations at Hutchins Group Campground please use this link: https://www.recreation.gov/camping/campgrounds/232266

Located just north of Bucks Lake Dam, this group campground is situated amongst the fir and pine trees off Bucks Lake. Hutchins Group Campground is a popular vacation spot in California's Plumas County. This group campground has three group campsites that accommodate up to 25 people each. The no-hookup sites feature tables, food lockers, fire rings with grill, potable water, and vault toilets. The group campsites are available by reservation only. Access to the group campground by large trailers and RVs is not advised due to the steep, narrow, and rugged access road. The group campground is part of Pacific Gas and Electric Co.'s hydropower license recreation area which centers around enticing Bucks Lake. The lake is home to five kinds of sport fish, and is a terrific place to swim, boat and water ski.

name: Kidd Lake Campground
description:
Kidd Lake Group Campground offers 10 sites in three separate clusters. Sites 1-5 are lakeside and can accommodate 30 people. Sites 6-7 can accommodate 12 people and sites 8-10 and can accommodate 18 people. Sites 6-7 and 8-10 are upland and a short hike from the shoreline. Each site contains two picnic tables and an outdoor pedestal barbecue. Potable water outlets, vault toilets and bear-proof food lockers are located close to each cluster. There is no kitchen facility, although, there is a shelter hut at the first site cluster.
 
Kidd Lake Campground is primarily a tent campground.  Each pod is allowed the number of cars equal to the number of sites (1-5=5, 6-7=2 and 8-10=3), plus one small RV (16 feet or less) per pod. There are no parking spurs at Kidd Lake Campground and RV's must remain in the parking lot.  A limited amount of overflow parking is available on a first-come first-served basis and is at the host discretion. 

Kidd Lake Campground is surrounded by the Tahoe National Forest, popular for outdoor recreation, the Tahoe National Forest has trails that take hikers, OHV riders and mountain bikers through a dazzling display of lakes, rivers and mountain tops. Located nearby is Long Lake, Serene Lake, Devils Peak and the Palisades Creek Trail to the North of the American River.  Due to the early pioneer and mining endeavors, historical sites, encampments, trails, wayside stations, and mines can be found throughout the forest opening a fascinating window into the past.

name: Lake McCumber Campground
description:
Lake McCumber Campground is a quiet, little campground located 40 miles east of Redding near the west entrance of Lassen Volcanic National Park on the McCumber Reservoir.  The campground is open year-round and has a total of 13 campsites, eight of the sites can accommodate RVs, trailers, and tents, while the other 5 are walk-in sites for tent camping only. Oaks provide ample shade at most sites.
Lake McCumber is a relaxing retreat for families and anglers alike. 

Area Attractions: The quarter mile-long lake is open to non-motorized boating such as kayaks and canoes. Campers enjoy swimming, hiking, or fishing for rainbow and brown trout. Drive to nearby Lassen Volcanic National Park. Watch for birds such as pileated woodpeckers, bald eagles, warblers, and western bluebirds.

Campsites have picnic tables and fire rings.  Vault toilets, drinking water and garbage receptacles are provided.  Lake McCumber Campground is easy to get to from Redding via Hwy 44.

name: Lake Spaulding Campground
description: Lake Spaulding Campground is located in the Sierra Nevada mountain range near Soda Springs, California. The lake is surrounded by giant granite boulders and thick pine forest. Lake Spaulding offers a range of water activities including all types of boating and there is a boat ramp which allows for easy access. Walk-in tent sites and a limited amount of overflow parking spots in the boat launch parking area are available. RV's and trailers longer than 30 feet are NOT recommended for sites in the campground loops. Drinking water, vault toilets and picnic areas are provided. Lake Spaulding Campground is included in the recreation area managed by Pacific Gas and Electric Co. in Northern California. Reservations for a campsite can be made using the convenient online system at (www.pge.com/recreation).

name: Last Chance Creek Campground  Closed 2026
description: pLast Chance Creek Campground is a great location for the whole family to enjoy the fun of Lake Almanor and Last Chance Creek in gorgeous Northern California. The secluded campground is close to where the creek empties into Lake Almanor well known for its beauty and wide range of activities. In the spring, keep an eye out for white pelicans, which make their home around the lake. Visitors will find 12 campsites, offered by first-come first-serve or through our on-line reservation system. There are no hookups but a double vault toilet is available. Group camping is also available at the Last Chance Creek Campground. There is 3 campsites which can accommodate up to 30, 40, or 60 people each. Each campsite has a fire ring, barbecue, wooden storage cabinets, and picnic tables. The spacious campground has piped water and vault toilets. A 2-night minimum stay is required. The campground has a horseshoe pit and a volleyball area. Horses are welcome in the group campground in sites #13-25. Bear boxes are not available at this location so please be prepared to lock your food in your car with the windows securely up.p

name: Lily Pad Campground
description: pNO RVs or TRAILERS! Lily Pad is set in the beautiful Sierra National Forest, Lily Pad Campground offers 15 campsites among pine trees and boulders. Guests have quick access to fishing and trails to the adjacent high country on the south end of Lake Wishon. Wishon Reservoir is popular for fishing and boating. With a 15 MPH speed limit, Wishon makes a great place for paddling kayaks, canoes and rafts. Trails lead into the John Muir wildernesses. At Lily Pad Campground, picnic tables, grills and vault toilets are available.p

name: Lodgepole Campground
description: Lodgepole Campground is located near the Lake Valley Reservoir, in Placer County. Online reservations can be booked to take advantage of the fishing, swimming and boating on the calm waters. The boating speed limit is under 10 miles per hour, which rules out water-skiing but benefits anglers. A trailhead from the campground leads south up Monumental Ridge to Monumental Creek, this is a good three-mile hike. Campsites can accommodate RV's up to 30 feet, however maneuvering through the campground does become difficult with RV's longer than 20 feet. Campground offers picnic tables, fire grills, drinking water and vault toilets.

name: Lower Blue Lake Campground
description: Lower Blue Lake Campground is a beautiful high-country campground at a popular trout angler location in Northern California. The Blue Lakes are part of a cluster of lakes near Hope Valley and are a premier destination for paddle boaters. The lakes offer boating, and fishing. One earthen boat ramp is available at Lower Blue Lake with adjacent trailer parking. Lower Blue Lake Campground has vault toilet facilities, piped water, picnic tables, fire rings and bear-proof food boxes.

name: Lower Bucks Campground
description: pLocated along the north shore of Lower Bucks Lake, this rustic campground is situated amongst the fir and pine trees and consists of seven scattered tent or small trailerRV with self-contained sewer systems sites. Lower Bucks Lake Campground is a popular vacation spot in California's Plumas County. The seven family campsites are available for First Come, First Serve camping, all with spectacular view of Lower Bucks Lake. Small RVs up to 20 feet in length can be accommodated on a few of the sites, which feature tables, food lockers, and fire rings with grill. There is one vault toilet available at a nearby day use area. No hookups or piped water available for the campsites. The native surface road to the campground is unimproved any may prove problematic for low-clearance vehicles and larger RVs. Lower Bucks Lake has a boat motor horsepower restriction ordinance by Plumas County that prohibits personal watercraft and water skiing on the reservoir. Canoeskayaks and small, low-horsepower fishing boats are allowed. The campground is part of Pacific Gas and Electric Co.'s hydropower license recreation area which centers around enticing Bucks Lake. Bucks Lake is home to five kinds of sport fish, and is a terrific place to swim, boat and water ski.ppp

name: Lower Lindsey Lake Dispersed Camping
description: Look forward to a relaxing day fishing and swimming at Lower Lindsey Lake Dispersed Camping. This remote campground has 12 rustic campsites for tent camping. Small watercraft like canoes, rafts and kayaks can be set in the water from the car-top boat launch. High clearance vehicles recommended. Hikers enjoy access to the Carr-Feeley trailhead. Picnic tables and vault toilets are provided.

name: Lower Rock Lake Dispersed Camping
description: Lower Rock Lake Dispersed Camping, offers just three rustic tent sites and is located near the Lindsey Lake Trailhead in the Tahoe National Forest.

name: Madesi River Access and Dispersed Camping
description:
Madesi River Access and Dispersed Camping

Located on the Pit River this accessible picnic area and accessible fishing pier are features of the Madesi River Access and Dispersed Campsites. Visitors can choose from seven sites in this Pacific Gas and Electric Co. campground in Shasta County. 

Since potable water, toilets and other amenities are not available, be sure to bring adequate water or be prepared to purify natural water sources before drinking. Camp at least 200 feet from springs, water, meadows, trails, and at least 50 feet from roads. 

Please remember: if you brought it in with you, then take it out when you leave (Pack It In/Pack It Out).

Madesi River Campground is non-reservable. It is First-Come First-Serve ONLY. Please select the Opening & Closing Dates icon to view the season dates.

name: Marmot Rock Campground
description:
Incredible views can be seen at Marmot Rock Campground, a high sierra campground located on Courtright Reservoir in the Sierra National Forest. A nearby boat ramp provides access to the reservoir, a pretty lake with opportunities for boating, with speed limits under 10 mph, and fishing. 

Campers are provided with picnic tables, grills, vault toilets, swivel-clasp-secured bear safe cabinets (one per campsite), but it does not have potable water at this time. 

The Courtright Reservoir, at 8,200 feet in elevation is located in one of the most superb geological areas of California. Bare granite domes rise from the shores of Courtright Reservoir and above the deep canyon cut by Helms Creek located at the north end of the lake. Ice Age glaciers sculpted the mountain peaks, slopes and valleys giving them their unique present-day shape. To the east Mt. Goddard rises majestically to 13,568 feet in elevation.

name: Meadow Lake Campground
description:
Meadow Lake Campground 
Meadow Lake is a beautiful high elevation lake in the Tahoe National Forest. Activities here include boating (small craft only), swimming or riding the nearby (OHV) trails. There is no garbage service provided, so please make sure that what you pack in, you pack out. There is no water available here either so, pack enough for cooking, dish-washing and drinking. If you have any questions or concerns, a campground host is onsite to assist you. Each site has a table, food locker and fire pit/grill combo.

Meadow Lake is also a popular spot for off-highway vehicle (OHV) enthusiasts as there are nearby trails to access. The Fordyce Jeep Trail and the annual Sierra Trek event in early August.  At that time, CA4WDC arranges with Pacific Gas & Electric to restrict water flow in Fordyce Creek to passable levels. Expert spotters and winches are provided at five critical points and no vehicle is ever left behind. The Fordyce Jeep Trail is 11.9 miles long. It begins at 12e45 Pierce OHV Trail and ends at Meadow Lake Forest Road 0843-017. The trail is open to all Off Highway Vehicles (OHV).  Recommended for experts only.

An informal boat launch provides access to Meadow Lake.

name: Middle Creek Campground
description: Middle Creek Campground is found along the meandering Middle Creek that connects Upper and Lower Blue Lakes. Middle Creek is a favorite among anglers. The nearby lakes offer boating, and fishing. Boat ramps are available at Upper and Lower Blue Lakes. Middle Creek Campground offers five camp sites for tents or RVs, sites 18 through 21 are along the creek and site 22 is across Blue lakes road next to the restroom which is ADA compliant. Campground includes vault toilets, piped water, picnic tables, fire-rings, and bear-proof food boxes.

name: Middle Creek Expansion Campground
description: Middle Creek Expansion Campground is a captivating spot in Alpine County, California, along the creek that connects the Upper and Lower Blue Lakes. The lakes offer boating, swimming and fishing. Unimproved boat ramps are available at both Upper and Lower Blue Lakes. There are 34 campsites for tents or RVs up to 45 feet, and amenities include vault toilets, piped water, picnic tables, grills and bear boxes. Across the road is Middle Creek Campground.

name: Middle Lindsey Lake Dispersed Camping
description: Pack your tent and hike the Lindsey Lake Trailhead to arrive at Middle Lindsey Lake Dispersed Camping. PG&E offers three rustic tent sites for those eager to explore the Tahoe National Forest. There is no garbage service provided, so please make sure that what you pack in, you pack out. There is no water available here either so, pack enough for cooking, dish-washing and drinking.

name: Mill Creek Campground
address: Mill Creek Road USFS Route 24N33 to 24N69X
description: ppnbspSituated along the fir and pine tree covered shore of Mill Creek is a deep, quiet inlet at the north end of Bucks Lake, Mill Creek Campground is a popular vacation spot in California's Plumas County. The 10 family campsites (two of which are walk-in) are available for first come, first serve camping. RVs up to 20 feet in length can be accommodated on a few of the sites. Sites feature tables, food lockers, fire rings with grill and are non-hookup. The campground includes vault toilets and piped water. Hiking is immediately available along the Mill Creek Trail, which is accessed from this campground via a short tie trail. The campground is part of Pacific Gas and Electric Co.'s hydropower license recreation area, which centers around enticing Bucks Lake. The lake is home to five kinds of sport fish, and is a terrific place to swim, boat and water ski.p

name: Navy Camp Campground
description:
Navy Campground is located at the end of Gravelly Valley Air Strip. A trail provides access to Lake Pillsbury in the Mendocino National Forest. Popular activities there include fishing, biking, canoeing, kayaking and hiking. Navy Campground, operated by Pacific Gas and Electric Co., has 20 campsites and double vault toilets.

Navy Campground is non-reservable. It is First-Come First-Serve ONLY. Please select the Opening & Closing Dates icon to view the season dates.

name: North Battle Creek Campground
description: North Battle Creek Campground on the North Battle Creek Reservoir, is a scenic spot in Shasta County. Limited to non-motorized boating, the lake, at 5,600 feet in elevation, is an ideal place for canoeing, kayaking and rafting. Ten no-hookup sites for RVs or tents are available, as well as five walk-in tent sites. North Battle Creek Campground opens as weather permits. Potable water, fire rings, bear safe trash cans and a dirt boat ramp are available. Road is rough and high clearance vehicles are recommended.

name: Northshore Campground
description: Boating and fishing are major draws to Northshore Campground, located in a wooded area near the shore of Lake Britton. Directly across the lake is McArthur-Burney Falls Memorial State Park, and it is a short drive to view Burney Falls. Northshore Campground, operated by Pacific Gas and Electric Co., contains 29 campsites for visitors to enjoy the sights.

name: Oak Flat Campground
description:
Oak Flat Campground is an overflow camping area with 12 designated campsites and additional dispersed campsites located in the Lake Pillsbury area of California's Mendocino National Forest. This will be a good spot to try if the other campgrounds around Lake Pillsbury are full. The Pacific Gas and Electric Co. campground provides picnic tables, fire grills and vault toilet, but no potable water.

Oak Flat Campground is non-reservable. It is First-Come First-Serve ONLY. Please select the Opening & Closing Dates icon to view the season dates.

name: Philbrook Campground
description: Enjoy the cedar trees and beautiful views at Philbrook Campground. Located in the Lassen National Forest, the Pacific Gas and Electric Co. campground provides fishing access and a short, paved, car-top boat launch with a gravel extension. There are double vault toilets available and non-potable water. The Lassen National Forest is a premier location for hiking and kayaking. There are no bear boxes on-site, please place all food items in vehicles at night in order to avoid bear issues.

name: Pit 5 Dam River Access and Camping Dispersed
description: The Pit 5 Dam River Access and Campsites is a remote campground in Shasta County. Four walk-in campsites without restrooms or other facilities make for a true back-to-nature experience in Northern California.

name: Pogie Point Campground
description:
Pogie Point Campground is located on the northwest corner of Lake Pillsbury. The lake is Mendocino National Forest's largest lake and is popular for swimming, fishing and boating.

Pogie Point Campground has 44 sites, best suited for tent camping. Campsites are well shaded by oaks and pines, although most campsites don't offer views of the lake, others have nice views of the lake and there is plenty of opportunity to swim, fish and boat. Nearby is a boat launch. Amenities include vault toilets, drinking water, picnic tables, food lockers, fire rings and grills are provided. No hook-ups.

Pogie Point Campground is non-reserveable. It is First-Come First-Serve ONLY. Please select the Opening & Closing Dates icon to view the season dates.

name: Ponderosa Flat Campground
description: Ponderosa Flat Campground is located in the ponderosa pine forest along the shores of Butt Lake in Northern California's Plumas County. Many of its sites are on the shoreline and several sites are now available by reservation using our online system. The rustic campsites do not have any hook-ups, but vault toilets, fire-rings, and potable water are available. There are no bear boxes present, so please remember to store all food items in vehicles overnight to avoid issues with bears. Canoeing, kayaking and sail boating are popular activities on the lake. Motorized fishing boats are allowed, but water skiing and jet skiing are not. A 30' height restriction, including mast is enforced. Nearby Ray Adams Boat ramp (approx. 1 mile south of CG) is a concrete, single lane ramp with no courtesy dock and limited trailer parking area. No launch fee is required.

name: Rocky Point Campground
description: Beautiful views of Lake Almanor and Mount Lassen can be seen from Rocky Point Campground, located among the Ponderosa Pines in Plumas County, one of Northern California's most scenic areas. Several campsites are available for reservations, which can be booked from our online system. Other sites remain first-come, first-served. Many of the camping spots are on the shoreline of Lake Almanor, best known for its boating, fishing and water-skiing. Biking or walking the paved Lake Almanor Recreation Trail reveals a wide variety of birds, beautiful scenery and boundless wildlife in the area.

name: Rucker Lake Dispersed Camping
description:
Fishing and swimming are great activities for Rucker Lake in the Tahoe National Forest. Walk down the path to seven walk-in sites. Picnic tables, grills, bear box food lockers and vault toilets are available. An unpaved road provides access to the gravel parking area.

Rucker Lake Dispersed Campground is non-reserveable. It is First Come First Serve ONLY. Please select the Opening & Closing Dates icon to view the season dates.

name: Ruling Creek Campground and River Access
description:
Ruling Creek Campground is a great place to camp if you're fly fishing. Built on the edge of the Pit River, it offers great access to the water. Ruling Creek Campground is a newer addition to Pacific Gas and Electric Co.'s many facilities located in Northern California and has eleven campsites.

Ruling Creek Campground is non-reservable. It is First-Come First-Serve ONLY. Please select the Opening & Closing Dates icon to view the season dates.

name: Smalley Cove Campground
description:
Walk-in available during non-reservation season. See Open/Close sheet on the homepage for dates. 

Smalley Cove Campground and Day Use Area is located on the Kerckhoff Reservoir, and is available for tent camping or day use. There are five campsites with picnic tables and barbecue grills. Fishing for eastern brook trout, small-mouth bass, bluegill and catfish is best done from the reservoirs shoreline, or on a canoe or float tube. Guests return again and again to enjoy the magnificent Sierra National Forest.

name: Sterling Lake Dispersed Camping
description:
Sterling Lake hike-in CG as Open for the season due to the anticipated road closure of Rd. 85 being canceled. 

4WD is recommended to access Sterling Lake Campground in the Tahoe National Forest. The campground has six walk-in sites. Sterling Lake is a great location for fishing and boating. A vault restroom is provided, but no garbage receptacles. Remember to pack in and pack out.	

Sterling Lake Dispersed Campground is non-reserveable. It is First Come First Serve ONLY. Please select the Opening & Closing Dates icon to view the season dates.

name: Sundew Campground
description: Located adjacent Bucks Lake Dam, this campground is situated amongst the fir and pine trees covering the shore at the north end of Bucks Lake. Sundew Campground is a popular vacation spot in California's Plumas County. The 21 family campsites are non-hookup and available for first come, first serve camping with spectacular views of Bucks Lake. RVs up to 30 feet in length can be accommodated on a few of the sites, which feature tables, food lockers, fire rings with grill, and piped water. The campground is part of Pacific Gas and Electric Co.'s hydropower license recreation area which centers around enticing Bucks Lake. The lake is home to five kinds of sport fish, and is a terrific place to swim, boat and water ski.

name: Sunset Point Campground
description:
Sunset Point Campground located on Lake Pillsbury in the Mendocino National Forest. Less than a quarter mile from the Pillsbury Pines Boat Launch and Day Use Area, Sunset Point is a great spot for fishing, swimming and boating. The adjacent Lakeshore Trail is a designated nature trail along the shore of the lake for hiking, biking and equestrian use. Campsites total 53, including 14 doubles, at this Pacific Gas and Electric Co. facility, and there is a double vault toilet.		

Sunset Point Campground is non-reserveable. It is First Come First Serve ONLY. Please select the Opening & Closing Dates icon to view the season dates.

name: Trapper Springs Campground
description:
Located on the west shore of Courtright Reservoir, Trapper Springs Campground is surrounded by conifer trees and granite rock. Courtright Reservoir offers boating, under 10 mph, and fishing. The area has many hiking opportunities at the nearby John Muir Wilderness and the Dinkey Lakes Wilderness. 

Courtright Reservoir, at 8,200 feet in elevation is located in one of the most superb geological areas of California. Bare granite domes rise from the shores of Courtright Reservoir and above the deep canyon cut by Helms Creek located at the north end of the lake. Ice Age glaciers sculpted the mountain peaks, slopes and valleys giving them their unique present-day shape. To the east Mt. Goddard rises majestically to 13,568 feet in elevation.

Trapper Springs Campground, a Pacific Gas and Electric Co. facility in the Sierra National Forest, has vault toilets, and potable water.

name: Trout Creek Campground
description: Trout Creek Campground, is located in the recreation area near Lake Pillsbury and the Eel River Basin. Located near the Eel River, Trout Creek Campground offers picnic tables, fire grills and a double vault toilet. Swimming,  and non-motorized boating are favorite activities in this Northern California location. Reservations may be made through the user-friendly online system. Small RVs and tents are allowed. Trout Creek Campground has no hookups, and trailers are not allowed in the lower loop.

name: Upper Blue Lake Campground
description: One of the best spots for fishing and paddle boating is Upper Blue Lake Campground, a beautiful high country area in California's Alpine County. Blue Lakes, a group of lakes near Hope Valley, are known for great fishing, boating and swimming. Upper Blue Lake Campground, run by Pacific Gas and Electric Co., is outfitted with vault toilets, piped water, picnic tables, fire rings and bear-proof food boxes. Look for earthen boat ramps at both the Upper and Lower Blue Lakes.

name: Upper Blue Lake Dam Site Campground
description: The Upper Blue Lake Dam Site Campground is set in the scenic high country of Alpine County, California. The lakes are known for terrific paddle boating and trout fishing, as well as swimming. Upper Blue Lake Dam Site Campground is one of many operated by Pacific Gas and Electric Co. in Northern California. On-site are vault toilets, piped water, picnic tables, fire rings and bear-proof food boxes. Nearby attractions include Hope Valley and the Pacific Crest Trail.

name: Upper Blue Lake Dam Site Expansion Campground
description: Upper Blue Lake Dam Site Expansion Campground, an amazing high country campground is a popular fishing spot. Blue Lakes, a cluster of lakes near Hope Valley in Northern California, are top-notch locations for paddle boating, fishing and swimming. At the campground, operated by Pacific Gas and Electric Co., visitors will find 15 campsites, vault toilets, piped water, picnic tables, fire rings and boxes to protect food from bears.

name: Upper Kings River Group Campground
description:
Located in the Sierra National Forest, along the Kings River, near the base of the Wishon Reservoir Dam. The campground offers space for up to 50 people in incredible surroundings. Wishon Reservoir is popular for fishing and boating. Only a short walk from the group campground are a number of wheelchair accessible fishing platforms along the Kings River. These platforms make the campground a great choice for anglers with mobility difficulties or for supervised small children who want to fish. Wishon Reservoir is popular for paddling kayaks, canoes and rafts. 

Nearby trails lead into the John Muir wildernesses. Named after the naturalist devoted to protecting and preserving some of this country's natural treasures, the area stretches 100 miles and encompasses snow-capped mountains, deep canyons and vast expanses of terrain carved by glaciers.

A public boat launching facility is available at the south end of the lake. Operated by Pacific Gas & Electric, the Upper Kings River Group Campground has 5 campsites which form a single group campground for up to 50 people. Each of the 5 campsites has 2 picnic tables, a fire ring, a lantern holder, and pads for 3 tents. There is a central food service area with 2 food preparation tables, 2 barbecue grills, and a food storage building. The group site also has a large fire ring with 10 benches. Bear in mind that this is bear country and food must be safely stored.

name: Upper Rock Lake Dispersed Camping
description:
Follow the signs to the Lindsey Lakes Trailhead in the Tahoe National Forest and discover the Upper Rock Lake. This small PG&E campground has just four hike-in sites.

Upper Rock Lake Dispersed Campground is non-reserveable. It is First Come First Serve ONLY. Please select the Opening & Closing Dates icon to view the season dates.

name: White Rock Lake Dispersed Camping
description: Take a hike to White Rock Lake in Nevada County, California. Six hike-in tent sites are available. 4WD recommended.
